position_sizing._notional_cap_note: Notional ceilings only. Risk-based sizing below is the binding constraint: a tight-stop setup may size up to these ceilings for the same 1% risk; a wide-stop setup sizes well under them. Raised from 10%/$1000 when risk-based sizing landed (2026-07-16). Rebased 10x DOWN on 2026-07-21 when the book was restated from a $10,000 start to a $1,000 start: every percentage stays identical, only the notional ceilings moved ($2000 -> $200, conviction $3000 -> $300, min clamp $200 -> $20). See _fractional_stop_note below — the smaller book changes what the broker can protect.

risk_based_sizing._note: Van Tharp / Elder / Turtle framework (research 2026-07-16, user-approved). Every BUY risks at most risk_per_trade_pct of equity measured entry-to-stop; the validator CLAMPS oversized proposals down to the risk budget rather than rejecting. Portfolio heat = sum over open positions of entry-basis committed risk max(0,(avg_cost-stop)*qty)/equity; new BUYs are rejected past portfolio_heat_cap_pct (user chose 8%; literature 6-10%). Theme cap: committed initial risk sharing one demand_driver <= theme_initial_risk_cap_pct. Entry-basis heat means trailed stops above cost free the budget (pyramiding into winners stays possible). momentum_unwind_risk_scale halves the risk budget when momentum_health flags an unwind.

scale_in._note: Adds allowed only into winners (price above blended cost, never averaging down), max 2 adds, combined exposure stays inside the per-name cap. Partial exits via sell_fraction in (0,1].

conviction_tier._note: When earned, conviction raises the RISK budget to 1.5% (and the notional ceilings accordingly); base tier stays 1%.

position_sizing._fractional_stop_note: CONSEQUENCE OF THE $1,000 BOOK, measured 2026-07-21 against the live 187-name universe. Alpaca carries fractional quantities only with time_in_force=day, so a GTC stop needs a whole-share leg (execution/alpaca_broker.py, MIN_WHOLE_SHARES_FOR_LIMIT=4 and _resting stop arming). At a $1,429 position (the $10,000 book) 69.5% of the universe got a full exchange-held GTC stop attached at entry and only 2.1% fell under one share. At a $143 position (this book) those become 3.2% and 72.2%: most entries are now sub-one-share, so their protective stop is a DAY order that expires at the close and is re-armed by scripts/stop_watch.py on the Actions cron. Intraday protection is a real resting broker order and is essentially unchanged; what is lost is the overnight/weekend leg, where the exit now depends on the poller's next tick rather than the opening print. Accepted deliberately: the gap risk is real but denominated in single-digit dollars at this size. Do NOT read a low whole-share count as a reason to skip a setup.

quality._min_rr_note: Raised 1.0 -> 2.0 (2026-07-16, user-approved after expectancy research): breakeven win rate at 2:1 is 33%, keeping the book profitable across the realistic 40-55% band; a 1:1 floor loses money below ~52% wins after costs (Minervini/O'Neil both demand ~2:1 at entry).
quality._volatility_stop_note: A stop tighter than the name's noise is not protection - it exits on ordinary volatility, not on a broken thesis. The stop must sit at least max(min_stop_atr_multiple x 14d-ATR%, min_stop_expected_move_fraction x options expected_move%) below entry. Enforced only when volatility data is present (fail-open). If that floor exceeds max_stop_loss_distance_pct, the name is too volatile for a valid swing stop and is rejected.
quality._trailing_stop_note: Chandelier exit (LeBeau/Elder; user-approved 2026-07-16): once a position's high-water mark puts (high_water - 3xATR) ABOVE the plan stop, the effective stop ratchets up with it - never down, never widened, and deliberately NO breakeven jump at +1R (research shows early breakeven moves gut trend expectancy). Forced exits fire on the effective stop; reason trailing_stop_breached when the trail was binding.
quality._falsifiability_note: ADDED 2026-07-19 (audit). variant_perception, scenarios and thesis_invalidators were PRESENCE-checked only, while CLAUDE.md twice called variant_perception 'validator-enforced' - a single non-space character satisfied it. min_invalidator_chars was 12, so 'drops below 50dma' (17) passed as a binding falsifier. scenarios' probabilities need not have summed to 1, and tools/scenario_ev.py computed honest EV whose only callers were two RENDERING paths. Now: invalidating_print needs a numeric threshold, time_box needs a date or day-count, variant_perception needs a figure and a dated resolution, and scenario probabilities must sum to ~1 with a non-negative probability-weighted return. These check SHAPE, not argument quality - no regex grades a thesis, and the risk desk and the reader remain the judges of that.

theme_risk._note: Market value of positions sharing the same demand_driver plus proposed size must stay under this fraction of equity. Catches DELL+HPE style single-factor books that sector caps miss when names sit in different GICS sleeves. Fail-open if demand_driver missing (field check already rejects). book_risk._tradeability_note: Added 2026-07-19, both DEFAULT OFF pending evidence. Both floors currently fail OPEN on missing data: a proposal on a ticker absent from market_context skips the stop noise-band check entirely (a 1% stop on an 8%-ATR name passes), and a name with no market-cap figure clears the $1B floor by default. The enforcement is built and tested; enabling is a one-line flip once the evidence is in. require_volatility_data: a live gather covers 182/187 tickers with ZERO universe names absent, so the coverage case is already strong - held off only because 26 existing tests pass market_context={} and rewriting that many safety fixtures hours before going live is how a real assertion gets weakened by accident. Blocking the whole book on a network blip is a worse failure than the fail-open it replaces, and the weekly universe review already bars sub-$1B names from entering. book_risk._note: Book-level risk (added 2026-07-19 after an audit found every binding constraint was arithmetic on ONE proposal while portfolio_beta / shared_left_tail / corr_to_book were computed by tools/correlation.py and consumed only as prose). Four controls, all in tools/book_risk.py, all pure. (1) max_factor_stack_pct: aggregate notional across factor_map.AI_STACK_DRIVERS. The 2% per-driver risk cap permits ~2 positions per driver, so 8 positions across 4 AI-stack drivers was 100% AI exposure passing every existing limit - a per-driver cap is not a factor cap. (2) gap_adjusted_heat: the 8% heat cap sums (cost-stop)*qty, which assumes stops FILL AT THE STOP - contradicted by execution_costs.stop_gap_atr_fraction (0.5) in this same file, and by the only closed stop in the ledger (DELL plan stop 408.00, fill 389.75, 4.5% through, realized -13.5% on a position sized for 1%). Heat now adds the modelled gap-through, using correlation only to decide how much of the book gaps on the same morning - NEVER to hand budget back, since the plain sum is already the fully-correlated case. Unknown correlation assumes the worst. (3) max_portfolio_beta: MV-weighted against EQUITY not invested capital, so a half-cash book reads as half-exposed. (4) stress_scenarios: named shocks priced against the book the proposal WOULD create; losses deliberately NOT floored at stops, because a shock worth naming is one where stops gap. driver_shocks key __ai_stack__ shocks the whole factor group. All four fail CLOSED on unverifiable inputs, matching the portfolio_heat_unverifiable precedent.

recent.topic: Estimate-revision momentum: how upward EPS/revenue revision breadth leads price via the post-forecast-revision drift, and why breadth + price-confirmation beats a lone divergence
recent.summary: Analyst estimate revisions are a genuine, well-documented fundamental predictor: prices underreact to revisions and DRIFT in their direction for roughly six months (the post-forecast-revision drift, PFRD). Old evidence (Givoly/Lakonishok-era) put the up-minus-down revision portfolio spread near ~3% annually, and later work finds aggregated revisions can predict post-earnings-announcement returns as well as or better than the earnings surprise itself. The mechanism is the reason it persists and is the key to trading it: the DIRECTION of revisions is far more persistent than the direction of returns because analysts themselves underreact — anchoring-and-adjustment and herding make them revise incrementally and insufficiently, so a first up-revision statistically predicts more up-revisions (Chen et al. 2020, JBFA). Signal quality is not uniform. A single revision is mostly noise, and noise/bias in analyst forecasts rises with the forecast horizon (Noise in Expectations, RFS 2024), so BREADTH — how many analysts are raising vs cutting over ~100 days — and NEAR-TERM (next-quarter/next-FY) revisions carry the real signal, not one far-out number. Consistency matters more than magnitude: high-innovation revisions that are CONSISTENT with the prior trend and with price action drive more drift than larger 'reversal' revisions that fight the tape (Chen 2025), and revisions that merely drift toward existing consensus ('low-innovation') carry little information. recent.topic: Exit on pre-committed invalidators, not real-time conviction: the disposition effect, 'resulting', and why the written plan (not the mood) must license every early exit
recent.summary: My single binding process_fail is HPE: I closed a LOSING position ahead of its stop on a 'conviction crack,' graded process_fail with tag missing_invalidators_on_plan. The behavioral literature explains why that class of decision loses systematically. Odean's canonical study of 10,000 brokerage accounts (Journal of Finance 53:1775-1798, 1998) documents the disposition effect: investors are 1.5-2x more likely to sell a winner than a loser, and crucially this is NOT justified by subsequent returns - the losers they clung to did not go on to outperform, so the discretionary exit judgment was simply wrong on average. The practitioner consensus fix is pre-commitment: a 1991 study found the disposition effect weakens sharply when people sell at predetermined rules/intervals instead of discretionarily, and the reliable antidotes are predefined exit rules set BEFORE entry, mechanical stop/target execution, and documenting the rationale so the exit is a rule-check rather than a fresh emotional decision. recent.topic: The pullback-continuation entry in a leading uptrend: buying the low-volume ('no-supply') dip to structural support instead of chasing the fresh high
recent.summary: The pullback-continuation setup buys a temporary dip inside an established uptrend rather than chasing a new high. It works because two well-documented return patterns run on different clocks: medium-term momentum persists over roughly 3-12 months while short-term returns (days to a few weeks) mean-revert (the short-term reversal effect, Blitz/Huij, Alpha Architect summaries). Buying the short-term dip in a medium-term leader therefore rides the durable trend while getting a better price and a tighter stop. The whole craft is separating a HEALTHY pullback -- shallow, orderly, on DRYING volume, the Wyckoff/VSA 'no supply' bar where professionals simply stop selling -- from a REVERSAL, which is sharp, wide-range, and comes on HIGH volume that breaks structure ('supply'). Volume is the tell, not price alone. Minervini's version: after a valid advance a healthy pullback retraces modestly (~8-10% max, or back to a rising 50-DMA), volume contracts into the dip and re-expands on the resumption; common support zones are the 20-EMA, 50-DMA, and the 38-62% Fibonacci band. Critically, the entry is the RESUMPTION, not the dip itself -- you wait for volume to dry up and then a confirming up-move, you do not catch the falling knife. This is the one thing my own 12-year ablation confirmed: no_supply_pullback scored +0.22pp (21d) / +0.25pp (63d), the only positive read among ~25 indicators tested, measured on names already above their 200-DMA. recent.topic: Correlation-adjusted position sizing: co-moving names are one bet (the effective-number-of-bets collapse), not many, and why that governs portfolio heat and the theme-risk cap
recent.summary: Diversification by COUNT is an illusion; only diversification by uncorrelated risk FACTORS reduces risk. For N equally-sized positions each with volatility sigma and pairwise correlation rho, portfolio volatility is sigma*sqrt([1+(N-1)*rho]/N): at rho=0 that is sigma/sqrt(N) (full benefit), but at rho->1 it goes to sigma, i.e. the N positions behave as ONE. The clean summary statistic is the effective number of independent bets, N_eff ~= N/[1+(N-1)*rho]; two names at rho~0.85 give N_eff~1.08 -- essentially a single bet. That is exactly my realized loss history: DELL and HPE were two tickers on ONE hyperscaler_server_capex driver, so a Meta-overbuild headline took both out at once, and my '2 positions' were 1 correlated bet the whole time. Attilio Meucci's Effective Number of Bets (exponential Shannon entropy of the diversification distribution) makes the same point formally: hidden correlation makes a book that LOOKS like N holdings act like ~1 exposure to one factor, and PCA can even hide this (minimum-torsion/factor framing is needed to see it). The Turtle system encoded the practitioner version as hard unit caps -- 4 units single market, 6 closely-correlated, 10 loosely, 12 in one direction -- precisely so a cluster of correlated trades could not become one oversized bet. Two cautions from the sources: (1) correlations RISE toward 1 in exactly the tail shock you are stopping for, so a benign-looking rho understates joint downside; (2) correlated stops fire and GAP together
recent.how_to_apply: Before any BUY, run the one-bet test using portfolio_risk and the demand_driver_map: if the candidate shares a holding's demand_driver OR shows corr_to_book > ~0.7, treat it as ADDING to an existing bet, not opening a new one -- size the pair against the THEME RISK <= 2% cap as a single position, never as two independent 1% risks (this is the DELL+HPE lesson made quantitative). recent.topic: Stop distance vs. holding horizon: the √t noise band, and why entry location (not stop width) is the binding lever on multi-week swings
recent.summary: A stop has one job: fire on evidence the thesis broke, not on ordinary noise. Kaminski & Lo (SIFR RR 63, 2008; J. Financial Markets 18(C):234-254, 2014) prove that under a random walk, stop-loss rules ALWAYS decrease expected return; they only add value when returns exhibit momentum/positive serial correlation, generating what they call a 'stopping premium' proportional to return persistence (empirically 50-100bp/month during stop-out periods, US equities 1950-2004). So a stop placed inside the random-walk noise band is a pure expected-return tax. The quantitative half comes from volatility scaling: noise excursion grows with the SQUARE ROOT of time, so a stop sized off a one-day ATR is roughly √N too tight for an N-day hold (√45 ≈ 6.7). Danielsson & Zigrand (J. Banking & Finance 30(10):2701-2713, 2006) show the √t rule is only valid under iid normal returns and under jump diffusion 'leads to a systematic underestimation of risk, whereby the degree of underestimation worsens with the time horizon [and] the jump intensity' — so for equities with earnings inside the horizon, ATR×√N is a FLOOR on the noise band, not a ceiling. The decisive consequence: NO static entry stop inside a 15% cap can cover a 45-day noise band. This is not a reason to widen stops (the cap and the 2:1 RR floor forbid it) — it is the proof that stop width is not the free lever. Entry location is. ANET.weight: Cycle position and inventory > headline P/E. Low fwd multiples at peak earnings are often traps.

lines.why: Earnings are mean-reverting; multiples look cheapest at the top.
lines.good_looks_like: Early/mid cycle: rising estimates, improving inventory, demand visibility (e.g. HBM).
lines.red_flag: Record margins/EPS with falling revisions — classic late cycle.

lines.why: Inventory build is the tell for semis.
lines.good_looks_like: Inventory stable or declining vs sales; supply discipline.
lines.red_flag: Inventory_building flag / channel fill while prices weaken.

lines.why: Cheap fwd P/E on peak EPS is not value.
lines.good_looks_like: Multiple reasonable vs mid-cycle earnings power, not peak.
lines.red_flag: Thesis is only 'cheapest in group' without cycle underwriting.

lines.why: GPU/hyperscaler buyers dominate some nodes.
lines.good_looks_like: Diversified end demand or multi-year capacity contracts.
lines.red_flag: One customer can cancel the cycle.

lines.why: Revisions lead the cycle more than price alone.
lines.good_looks_like: Revisions up or stabilizing after a washout.
lines.red_flag: Revisions still rolling over into a bounce.

GE.label: Quality compounder / broad-market leader (default quality screen)

lines.why: Compounders buy back stock and fund growth from ops.

lines.why: Need growth to support the multiple.

lines.why: Net debt / leverage must be sane.
lines.good_looks_like: Net cash or modest net debt / EBITDA.
lines.red_flag: Leverage spike without earnings power.

lines.why: Moat shows up in margins.

lines.red_flag: Structural margin decay.

lines.why: Quality is not always cheap.
lines.good_looks_like: Multiple reasonable vs growth and history.
lines.red_flag: Top-decile multiple with slowing growth.

lines.why: Revisions drive near-term swings.
lines.good_looks_like: Flat to up.
lines.red_flag: Cuts into elevated expectations.

lines.red_flag: Street still cutting hard.
